intro_html: Kofta is spiced beef shaped into little logs and roasted until browned, then served over rice with cool garlic tzatziki, tomatoes, and herbs. It is a serious flavor-per-effort bargain. Each bowl carries a hefty 47 grams of protein for about $3.86, on the higher end for us but still less than a third of the restaurant plate.
cost_closing_html: About $3.86 a bowl for a kofta plate that runs $15 or more at a Mediterranean grill. This is one of our pricier bowls, and it still beats eating out by more than $11 a plate.
shop_smart: Cherry tomatoes were the second biggest line on this receipt at over $10. If romas or regular tomatoes are cheaper the week you shop, dice those instead and save a few dollars.
Making tzatziki from a big tub of plain Greek yogurt costs a fraction of the little store-made tubs, and the 32 ounce tub covered all 14 servings for under $3.
Beef is the anchor at nearly $29. Watch for the 5 pound value pack price and cook this recipe the week it drops.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the tzatziki: grate about a third of the cucumbers, salt them, and squeeze out the water hard. Stir into the Greek yogurt with half the garlic, a splash of lemon juice, the mint, and a pinch of salt. Refrigerate.
Cook the rice: 4.5 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Grate one of the red onions and squeeze it dry. Mix it into the ground beef with the remaining garlic, cumin, cinnamon, allspice, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper.
Shape the beef into small logs or ovals, about 3 per serving, and set them on foil-lined sheet pans.
Broil or bake at 450 F for 12 to 15 minutes, flipping once, until browned outside and cooked through with no pink in the center.
Slice the remaining cucumber and red onion and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Build each bowl: rice, kofta, tomato and cucumber salad, cilantro on top, tzatziki in its own corner or cup.
portion_html: Weigh your finished kofta in the pot, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14, then do the same for the rice. Each assembled bowl lands at 562 calories and 47 grams of protein.

head.description: Middle Eastern beef kofta bowls with tzatziki: 562 calories and 47g protein at about $3.86 a serving. Spiced kofta, rice, and cool tzatziki, 14 bowls.
head.keywords: beef kofta bowls, kofta with tzatziki, middle eastern meal prep, high protein rice bowls, homemade tzatziki recipe, budget kofta recipe
steps: Make tzatziki: squeeze grated salted cucumber dry, then mix with Greek yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, and mint. Chill.
Mix beef with squeezed grated onion, garlic, and the spices, then shape into small logs.
Broil or bake at 450 F for 12 to 15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Assemble 14 bowls with rice, kofta, tomato cucumber salad, cilantro, and tzatziki on the side.
